verdicts.reason: rankScores takes number[] and returns number[], but calls scores.sort() with no comparator, so the numbers are coerced to strings and ordered lexicographically ([10, 9, 100] -> [10, 100, 9]); .reverse() then yields a wrong 'descending' ranking. Identical to the fixed topOrderTotals case and the same fix applies: scores.sort((a, b) => a - b).reverse(). (The sibling sortedPlayerNames is fine since default sorting is correct for strings.)
